Thanks for the demo this morning — quick recap and asks from our side.

Highlights: we liked the streaming latencies and the KV caching demo; main goals for the pilot are:
- Replace current retrieval+heuristic ranking for support triage with an LLM scoring layer (tight 200ms p95 target for single-turn inference at 2 RPS steady, spikes to 20 RPS allowed)
- Keep hallucination rate low for entity extraction and follow-up suggestion flow
- Budget target: ~$0.08 per 1k tokens for the production pilot (including padding/overhead)

As next steps we'd like:
1) A recommended pilot slate (2–3 models) with clear tradeoffs (quality vs latency vs unit cost)
2) Benchmark links and the prompt sets you used for the demo
3) Any quick guardrails / regression checks we should bake into the pilot (prompt tests, exact-match thresholds, etc.)

Attaching our short product requirements and a sample of historical support threads. Can you confirm what you'd recommend for a 6-week pilot?

Attachments: novus-prod-requirements.pdf (27KB)

Thanks,
Claire

Claire — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the requirements. Short answer: yes, we can run a 6-week pilot that meets your goals. Below is a recommended slate and the rationale plus links to the benchmark sheets and prompt pack.

Recommended pilot slate (start -> fallback):
1) rwd-medium-16B-32k-q4_0 (recommended pilot leader)
   - Why: best balance for short-form instruction-following and extraction at moderate cost. Quantized to q4_0 for memory efficiency; supports 32k context for future extensions.
   - Expected p95 latency (single token) on our Dedicated inference node: ~95–120ms; end-to-end single-turn (avg 350 tokens) ~120–180ms.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$0.06 per 1k tokens (inferred from dedicated pricing model).
   - Notes: lowest hallucination vs smaller variants in our internal evals for entity extraction.

2) rwd-small-6B-8k-zz (leader for ultra-low-cost throughput)
   - Why: lower cost option for high-throughput non-sensitive queries where some degradation in nuance is acceptable.
   - Expected p95 latency: ~40–60ms single-token; end-to-end single-turn ~60–85ms.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$0.018 per 1k tokens.
   - Notes: conservative — use for batch reranking or pre-filtering.

3) opt-66b-8k-quant (fallback for edge-case quality)
   - Why: when highest-quality, long-form reasoning is required; heavier cost/latency but better on tricky extractions.
   - Expected p95 latency: ~210–300ms single-token; end-to-end ~300–500ms depending on concurrency.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$0.22 per 1k tokens.

Tradeoff summary (quality / latency / cost):
- Leader (rwd-medium-16B): best quality-to-cost for your extraction use case; meets quality targets with moderate latency.
- Small (rwd-small-6B): very low cost and latency; suitable for pre-filtering/ranking.
- Opt-66b: high-quality fallback for ambiguous or high-risk tickets, used sparingly.

Benchmarks & prompt sets
- Prompt pack (pilot_prompt_pack_v1.zip): cleaned, instrumented prompts + neg-examples used in demo.
- Benchmark CSV (benchmarks_novus_5_22.csv): inference runs we did on samples you sent (precision/recall/hallucination rate/time-to-first-byte).
- Live link to repo: https://drive.redwood.ai/novus/benchmarks_0522

Quick guardrails we recommend embedding in pilot:
- Exact-match check for entity extraction where applicable (case-normalized)
- Response-content verifier: block list + entity schema checker; failover to deterministic extractor if confidence < 0.6
- Regression suite: 120 prompt-set checks (included in prompt pack) to run weekly, threshold-based alerts to us and to your SREs.

Attachments: pilot_prompt_pack_v1.zip, benchmarks_novus_5_22.csv

Proposed next steps
- We can run the pilot on Dedicated capacity (recommended) — Ben will follow up with a 6-week pricing estimate and a short SOW.
- If this looks good, I suggest a 30m follow-up tomorrow to agree on rollout gates and instrumentation.

Cheers,
